names.name: The murals
names.th: จิตรกรรมฝาผนัง
names.said: What a painting of a tattoo is evidence of

text.what: Northern temple walls carry men with marked legs and torsos, painted by people who saw them daily.
text.story:
The Lanna volume rests its case on exactly this: the evidence for the custom is the murals in important temples, which show men tattooed until they look dressed.

*Inference —* a mural is good evidence for three things — that the custom existed, roughly what area of the body it covered, and that it was ordinary enough to paint without comment. It is weak evidence for the designs themselves: painters simplify, and a wall painted with a hundred figures is not a pattern book. This site reads the murals for extent and does not read them for detail.

text_th.what: ผนังวัดทางเหนือมีภาพชายที่มีลายบนขาและลำตัว วาดโดยคนที่เห็นของจริงทุกวัน
text_th.story: *อนุมาน —* จิตรกรรมเป็นหลักฐานที่ดีสำหรับสามเรื่อง คือธรรมเนียมนี้มีจริง คลุมร่างกายราวไหน และเป็นเรื่องธรรมดาพอที่จะวาดโดยไม่ต้องอธิบาย แต่อ่อนสำหรับตัวลายเอง

names.name: The sample book
names.said: Burma, 1882 — flash, before the word existed

text.what: A book of drawings a Burmese tattooist carried, so the boy could pick his figures and their positions before the work started.
text.story:
Shway Yoe: "The best *sayas* carry about sample-books with them containing clever drawings, from which the aspirant may select the patterns he likes best, and mark their relative positions before he takes the opium."

That is a flash sheet, a consultation and a layout, in 1882, in a tradition usually described as though the designs came out of nowhere.

names.name: The stencil book
names.th: แบบสักยันต์สำหรับลอกลาย
names.said: A Thai book of yant designs, for tracing

text.what: A volume in the corpus this site counted is exactly what its title says: yant patterns for tattooists to trace.
text.story:
Its first page reads *แบบสักยันต์ · แบบยันต์ต่างๆ · สำหรับช่างสัก* — tattoo-yant patterns, various yant patterns, for tattooists. The plates are columns of Khom-script medallions under finials, birds facing each other into a heart shape, script down both sides.

*Inference —* the existence of a tracing book is the same fact as the Burmese sample book and the Bornean carved block: the repertoire is stored outside anybody's head, and it is stored in the form that transfers to skin.
